newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices sink with crude, weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices sink with crude, weather.

text.p: U.S. spot resid prices notionally lost ground Monday though few deals were done, as waning tensions between the U.S. and Iraq sharply pressured crude and drove fuel buyers to the sidelines, traders said.

"We were up last week on all the hype over crude. Now what fills the void? It's certainly not demand," said one cash trader, noting unseasonably-mild East Coast weather this week and still-cheap natgas continued to temper utility fuel oil needs.
In New York Harbor, one percent slipped 25-50 cents to $18.50-75 a barrel.
NYMEX October crude futures settled Monday $1.32 lower at $23.19 a barrel.
NYH high sulphurs fell 50-75 cents, with 2.2 percent now quoted in the low-$17 area, traders said.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, prices also were weaker, with one percent down more than 50 cents to $16.75-17.00 and three percent more than a quarter lower at about $16.50.
With typically-weak autumn demand ahead and gas still siphoning demand, few expected a significant rally in resid unless crude staged a sharp rebound.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
